text: cortex: a candidate body must stay inside the function it replaces. Every proposal is spliced in memory and the target re-located with the same lexer-aware locator (strings, raw strings, line and block comments read as the Axon lexer reads them) before caps, compile or any check; the target must end exactly where the body does and `fn <symbol>(` must occur in code as often as before. A body that closes the function and appends items (an injected @[test] ran under a whole-file fence that left fs:write open) or opens what it does not close is a non-terminal outside_symbol rejection (action_denied body_outside_symbol, feedback note naming the symbol), skipped by the early-stop streak, nothing written; `execute` applies the same rule at the write. A candidate the static walker cannot classify is refused as capability:unknown.
